chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: First European trip in 1954; the boy who knew his career
summary: Royal's first overseas trip, to Scandinavia and Western Europe, and an 11-year-old who recited his recording history.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When did you first start (inaudible), Basie?
When did you first start going into other countries?
With Basie, I took my first trip overseas in '54.
Went to Scandinavia. No, England wasn't allowing bands in at that time. We went to Scandinavia and Western Europe, Germany, Holland and those places like that.
That's all right. I took it as it came. It was good, an experience. I liked a lot of it because the people were very appreciative.
They were pretty well-versed in music,

I walked up on a child on a street one day. He was about 11 years old, in one of the countries -- I don't know whether it was Holland or whether it was in Germany -- and he walked up to me, out of clear blues and said, "Hello, Mr. Royal." I says, "Hello, young man. How are you?" He said, "Just fine." He says, "I know you very well." I says, "You do?" He says, "Yes," he says, "I've read about you." And he says, "You played at Sebastian's Cotton Club when you wasa young man and you worked with Curtis Moseby and you made such and such a record at such and such a date and you worked with this person here." I said, "How do you know these things?" He says, "I love jazz and I study that." He told me more about myself than I could remember just offhand and this boy was about 11 or 12 years old.

That showed me the appreciation that some people in foreign countries took to jazz. When this little child walked up to me and knew more about me than any fellow on the street in America, I was astounded.
